kaps_punt: Die Europese Renaissance 15de en 16de eeu: 'n keerpunt in die Europese geskiedenis

items.bewering: Renaissance is 'n woord wat hergeboorte of herlewing beteken.
items.bron: Britannica, 'What does the word Renaissance mean?' (britannica.com/question/What-does-the-word-Renaissance-mean): French for 'rebirth'; Vasari used Italian 'rinascita' (rebirth) in 1550. 'Herlewing' (revival) matches Britannica's 'revival of Classical learning'.

items.bewering: Die Renaissance het in die 15de en 16de eeu in Europa gebeur.
items.bron: CAPS Gr 6 SW, Geskiedenis Kwartaal 2 (gedrukte bl. 43) uses exactly this dating; Britannica Dictionary and OED give the wider span 14th-17th century, beginning in Italy in the 14th century. The sentence says it happened in the 15th and 16th centuries, which is true of the period's core; it does not claim those are its only centuries, so it is not contradicted. Noted for a person only: the lesson nowhere says it began in the 14th century in Italy.

items.bewering: Mense het opnuut na die boeke van die ou Grieke en Romeine gekyk. Hulle wou weet wat daardie mense geweet, gemaak en gebou het.
items.bron: Britannica Q&A on the Renaissance: the period was marked by a revival of Classical learning and wisdom, with new art and architecture; Britannica (Brunelleschi) on architects studying Roman buildings and Vitruvius.

items.bewering: Dit beteken nie dat mense voor hierdie tyd niks geleer het nie. Europa het toe al sy eie skole en sy eie geleerdes gehad.
items.bron: Britannica, 'University' and 'Scholasticism': Bologna (late 11th century), Paris (c. 1150-1170, from the Notre-Dame cathedral schools) and Oxford (by the end of the 12th century) existed well before the Renaissance, with cathedral and monastic schools before them.

items.bewering: Die herlewing het in die ryk handelstede van Italië begin.
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum Heilbrunn Timeline, 'Florence and Central Italy, 1400-1600' and 'Venice and Northern Italy, 1400-1600'; Britannica Dictionary ('especially in Italy'); OED via Perlego (began in Italy).

items.bewering: Die handelaars daar het met ver plekke handel gedryf en baie geld gemaak.
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum Heilbrunn Timeline: the Medici, a family of merchants and bankers, rose to virtual rule of Florence through their wealth; Bardi and Peruzzi banking families of Florence. Florence, Venice and Genoa grew rich on Mediterranean trade (general consensus across the sources returned).

items.bewering: 'n Kunstenaar of 'n geleerde moet ook elke dag eet en slaap. Ryk handelaars en die leiers van die stad het kunstenaars en geleerdes vir hulle werk betaal. So kon party mense hulle hele dag aan kuns en kennis wy.
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum Heilbrunn Timeline: Giovanni Rucellai paid Alberti to build the Palazzo Rucellai; the bankers' guild commissioned Ghiberti's St Matthew; the Medici's wealth made them central to humanist learning and the arts; Smarthistory 'Types of Renaissance patronage' (patrons included rulers, merchants, clergy, confraternities). The lesson does not say merchants and city leaders were the only patrons, so the Church's role is not contradicted by omission.

items.bewering: By baie vrae het mense voorheen die antwoord in 'n ou boek gesoek. Hulle het gaan kyk wat 'n ou skrywer of 'n leermeester daaroor gesê het. Vir baie mense was daardie woorde dan die antwoord.
items.blok: 'n Nuwe manier om 'n vraag te antwoord
items.bron: Britannica, 'History of science - The rise of modern science': for centuries the authority of Aristotle in dynamics, Ptolemy in astronomy and Galen in medicine had been taken for granted. The lesson's 'by baie vrae' and 'vir baie mense' keep it from claiming nobody observed before.

items.bewering: In hierdie tyd het al hoe meer mense begin om self te gaan kyk en te meet. Hulle het geteken wat hulle sien en opgeskryf wat hulle tel. Daarna het hulle weer gevra of die ou antwoord regtig klop.
items.blok: 'n Nuwe manier om 'n vraag te antwoord
items.bron: Britannica, 'History of science': beginning in the 16th century the authority of Aristotle, Ptolemy and Galen was challenged; Leonardo observed a mortar bomb's path and insisted it did not follow Aristotle's two straight lines; Metropolitan Museum essay 'Anatomy in the Renaissance' (artists' dissections and drawings c. 1500-1510 surpassed what universities taught).

items.bewering: Party kere het hulle met hulle eie oë iets anders gesien as wat in die ou boek gestaan het. Dan was dit die ou boek wat verkeerd was.
items.blok: 'n Nuwe manier om 'n vraag te antwoord
items.bron: Vesalius, De humani corporis fabrica (1543), corrected many errors in Galen's anatomy that came from dissecting animals (e.g. the lobed liver of pigs): Encyclopedia.com 'Vesalius'; EBSCO Research Starter 'Andreas Vesalius'; Wikipedia 'De Humani Corporis Fabrica'. 'Party kere' is accurate: Vesalius also kept some of Galen's errors.

items.bewering: Hierdie verandering is een rede waarom hierdie tyd as 'n keerpunt in die Europese geskiedenis gesien word.
items.blok: 'n Nuwe manier om 'n vraag te antwoord
items.bron: Britannica, 'History of science - The rise of modern science' (the overthrow of ancient authority from the 16th century); the Britannica Q&A notes Michelet and Burckhardt established the Renaissance as the period heralding the modern age. CAPS itself calls it 'n keerpunt. 'Een rede' is appropriately qualified.

items.bewering: Die herlewing van die ou Grieke en Romeine se boeke het in dieselfde tyd gebeur.
items.blok: 'n Nuwe manier om 'n vraag te antwoord
items.bron: Britannica Q&A on the Renaissance: revival of Classical learning was part of the same period.

items.bewering: Skilders het die wêreld so geskilder soos die oog dit werklik sien. 'n Pad op so 'n skildery word al hoe kleiner na agter toe. Ons noem dit perspektief.
items.bron: Smarthistory, 'Early applications of linear perspective' (Brunelleschi's experiment c. 1415-1420; lines converging on a vanishing point); Perspective Research Centre (Alberti's Della pittura, 1435). Mapping checked: linear perspective imitates how distant things appear smaller to the eye; a learner reasoning on from it (further away looks smaller, parallel lines meet) is led nowhere false.

items.bewering: Lig en skaduwee laat 'n gesig op 'n plat skildery nie plat lyk nie.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Chiaroscuro': a technique representing light and shadow as they define three-dimensional objects, brought to its full potential in European painting by Leonardo da Vinci in the late 15th century; Smarthistory, 'Chiaroscuro explained'.

items.bewering: Boumeesters het geboue ontwerp met pilare en boë soos dié van die ou Romeine.
items.bron: Britannica Students, 'Filippo Brunelleschi', and Britannica, 'Ospedale degli Innocenti': revival of ancient Roman forms including the column and the round arch; free-standing columns carrying round-arched arcades. Comparison checked: 'soos dié van die ou Romeine' maps form, not identity, which is correct (Britannica notes Romanesque roots too, which the lesson does not deny).

items.bewering: Mense het die menslike liggaam, plante, water en die sterre al eeue lank bestudeer. In hierdie tyd het party mense dit op nuwe maniere bestudeer.
items.bron: Britannica, 'History of science' (Galen in medicine and Ptolemy in astronomy, centuries old, challenged from the 16th century); Metropolitan Museum essay 'Anatomy in the Renaissance' (new anatomical study by artists including Leonardo). 'Party mense' is appropriately narrow.

items.bewering: Ver van land af kan 'n seevaarder nie die kus sien nie.
items.blok: Hoekom dit by hierdie onderwerp hoort
items.bron: Oxford History of Science Museum, 'The mariner's astrolabe and Portuguese exploration' (cabinet.ox.ac.uk/node/7661): out of sight of land, open-ocean navigators fixed latitude by astronomical observation rather than coastal landmarks.

items.bewering: In hierdie tyd is tabelle oor die son gedruk.
items.blok: Hoekom dit by hierdie onderwerp hoort
items.bron: Abraham Zacuto's Almanach perpetuum, printed at Leiria, Portugal, in 1496 (Latin translation by José Vizinho), with tables of the sun's position (Christie's catalogue; Journal for the History of Astronomy article, journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0021828619864472); the earliest surviving Portuguese regimento with solar declination tables printed in Lisbon c. 1509 (Oxford History of Science Museum).

items.bewering: Seevaarders het sulke tabelle op see gebruik om uit te werk hoe ver noord of suid hulle was.
items.blok: Hoekom dit by hierdie onderwerp hoort
items.bron: Oxford History of Science Museum, 'The mariner's astrolabe and Portuguese exploration': regimentos with solar tables and instructions were used with the astrolabe to find latitude from the noon sun. The Journal for the History of Astronomy article notes Zacuto's tables gave the sun's longitude, from which declination was derived; the lesson's 'tabelle oor die son' and 'sulke tabelle' cover both, so it is not contradicted.

items.bewering: Dit is een van die redes waarom skepe uit Europa so ver kon vaar, maar nie die enigste nie.
items.blok: Hoekom dit by hierdie onderwerp hoort
items.bron: Negated superlative ('nie die enigste nie'), checked as such. Oxford History of Science Museum (astronomical navigation with the astrolabe and solar tables enabled Portuguese voyages south of the equator, where the Pole Star cannot be used); other factors such as the magnetic compass and the caravel are named by CAPS Gr 6 Kwartaal 2 itself, so 'een van die redes ... nie die enigste nie' is accurate.

items.bewering: Lank voor hierdie veranderinge in Europa was daar al 'n groot en goed georganiseerde samelewing in Suider-Afrika: Mapungubwe
items.bron: SA History Online, 'Kingdoms of southern Africa: Mapungubwe' (sahistory.org.za/article/kingdoms-southern-africa-mapungubwe): trading centre c. 1220-1300, population around 5 000, regarded as the first class-based society in southern Africa; UNESCO's listing statement (quoted by the same sources; UNESCO page itself returned 403) calls it the centre of the largest kingdom in the subcontinent before it was abandoned in the 14th century. The changes the lesson describes (perspective c. 1415, printed solar tables 1496, Vesalius 1543) fall 100-300 years later, so 'lank voor' holds.

items.bewering: waarvan jy in Kwartaal 1 geleer het
items.bron: CAPS Sosiale Wetenskappe Gr 4-6 (KABV), gedrukte bl. 42: Graad 6 Geskiedenis Kwartaal 1 is 'n Afrika-koninkryk lank gelede in Suider-Afrika: Mapungubwe.

items.bewering: Renaissance: Die herlewing van die ou Grieke en Romeine se kennis en kuns.
items.bron: Britannica Q&A on the Renaissance (revival of Classical learning, art and architecture); Britannica Dictionary (period when interest in ancient art and literature revived). Read alone it is a standard, true definition.

items.bewering: keerpunt: 'n Punt waarna dinge anders as voorheen gebeur of gedoen word.
items.bron: Vocabulary.com (Dutch 'keerpunt', the same word): an event marking an important historical change of course; Interglot: turning point, watershed.

items.bewering: geleerde: Iemand wat baie studeer en baie oor 'n vak weet.
items.bron: Wiktionary 'geleerde' (Afrikaans noun, plural geleerdes); Interglot (Dutch 'geleerde': scholar, learned person).

items.bewering: perspektief: 'n Manier van teken of skilder waarin dinge wat ver weg is, kleiner lyk.
items.bron: Smarthistory, 'Early applications of linear perspective': a system for depicting depth on a flat surface in which objects diminish in size with distance toward a vanishing point.

opsomming: Every checkable claim held up against sources, including the printed solar tables, Vesalius correcting the old books and Mapungubwe being long before; the only nuance worth a person's glance is that the lesson uses CAPS's 15th-16th century dating while most references start the Italian Renaissance in the 14th century, which the lesson does not contradict.
